item.title: Fourth suspect surrenders over Nadi taxi driver robbery
item.description: The fourth suspect wanted for questioning in relation to an aggravated robbery involving a taxi driver in Nadi has surrendered to Police. The 25-year-old surrendered at the Vatuwaqa Police Post yesterday evening.
item.content:encoded:
The fourth suspect wanted for questioning in relation to an aggravated robbery involving a taxi driver in Nadi has surrendered to Police.

The 25-year-old surrendered at the Vatuwaqa Police Post yesterday evening.

His surrender follows the arrest of two other suspects who were taken into custody yesterday morning.

The first suspect had surrendered to Police on Tuesday after a video of the alleged robbery went viral on social media.

Police say investigations into the case are continuing.

item.title: Ro Filipe condemns attack on Nadi taxi driver, urgers drivers to prioritise their safety
item.description: The attack on a taxi driver in Nadi has been condemned by Minister for Transport, Ro Filipe Tuisawa who says Public Service Vehicle drivers provide an essential service and should not have to risk their lives, safety or livelihoods while carrying out their duties. Ro Filipe says taxi drivers and other PSV operators play a vital role in keeping Fiji moving, providing daily transport for thousands o
item.content:encoded:
The attack on a taxi driver in Nadi has been condemned by Minister for Transport, Ro Filipe Tuisawa who says Public Service Vehicle drivers provide an essential service and should not have to risk their lives, safety or livelihoods while carrying out their duties.

Ro Filipe says taxi drivers and other PSV operators play a vital role in keeping Fiji moving, providing daily transport for thousands of people travelling to and from work, schools, businesses, health services and other destinations.

He says PSV drivers work hard to earn a living while providing an essential service to the public, and they should be able to carry out their duties without fear that a routine passenger interaction or disagreement could put their safety, lives or livelihoods at risk.

The Minister has expressed concern over the circumstances surrounding the recent incident in Nadi.

Ro Filipe says our PSV drivers are members of our communities and they are parents, family members and individuals working hard to provide for their families.

He says there is absolutely no justification for violence or criminal behaviour against them.

Ro Filipe also reminded the public that PSV drivers are required to provide services in accordance with the conditions of their permits and should not unlawfully refuse service to members of the public.

He adds that while the conditions of a PSV permit require drivers to provide service to the public, drivers must also be able to exercise sound judgement when they genuinely believe their personal safety is at risk.

Ro says no driver should feel compelled to remain in a situation where they reasonably fear for their life or safety.

item.title: Flooding outside MHCC continues to disrupt commuters, authorities to work on permanent solution – Boseiwaqa
item.description: Persistent flooding outside MHCC in Suva continues to cause problems for pedestrians and commuters, particularly people trying to hail taxis during heavy rain. The area has experienced repeated flooding whenever there is significant rainfall, with the drainage system unable to cope with the water.
item.content:encoded:
Persistent flooding outside MHCC in Suva continues to cause problems for pedestrians and commuters, particularly people trying to hail taxis during heavy rain.

The area has experienced repeated flooding whenever there is significant rainfall, with the drainage system unable to cope with the water.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Suva City Council CEO Tevita Boseiwaqa says the affected underground drainage was cleared on Tuesday.

He says authorities are now looking at a permanent solution, which may require infrastructure changes.

Boseiwaqa says the Fiji Roads Authority is assessing the required work, while the Water Authority of Fiji may also need to be involved.

He says the Council will need to meet with the two authorities to determine the best long-term solution to address the persistent flooding.

Boseiwaqa says while the drainage has been cleared, more work is needed to prevent the problem from recurring.

item.title: FTA calls on Education Ministry to reverse revocation of 20-plus acting heads appointments
item.description: The Fijian Teachers Association is calling on the Ministry of Education to reconsider the revocation of acting appointments of more than 20 heads of schools in the Suva Education District, saying the affected teachers should not be made to suffer for the Ministry’s failure to fill the positions on time. FTA General Secretary Paula Manumanunitoga says the issue was one of the most pressing matters
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Teachers Association is calling on the Ministry of Education to reconsider the revocation of acting appointments of more than 20 heads of schools in the Suva Education District, saying the affected teachers should not be made to suffer for the Ministry’s failure to fill the positions on time.

FTA General Secretary Paula Manumanunitoga says the issue was one of the most pressing matters raised by teachers during the Association’s Annual Delegates Conference.

Manumanunitoga says some of the affected teachers had been acting as heads of schools for several years, with one serving in an acting position for about four years before receiving a letter last week revoking the appointment.

He says acting positions are not supposed to remain vacant for more than six months and should be advertised within that period to allow qualified candidates to apply and the most meritorious candidate to be appointed.

However, Manumanunitoga says the Ministry allowed some of these teachers to continue acting for one, two, three and even four years .

Insert: Manumanunitoga on victimised 26th Aug 26

Manumanunitoga says the teachers had moved into higher salary brackets while acting in the senior positions, and some would have made financial commitments based on those salaries, including car loans and household purchases.

He says returning them to their substantive positions would mean a significant reduction in their salaries and could leave some struggling to meet their financial commitments.

The FTA General Secretary says the matter was discussed through a motion at the conference, which was carried by delegates.

He says the Association will now ask the Ministry to stop revoking the acting appointments, allow the affected teachers to remain in their positions for the time being and advertise the vacant posts as quickly as possible so qualified teachers can apply.

Manumanunitoga says where a confirmed head of school has already been appointed to take over a position, the Ministry should also consider moving the affected acting head to a similar vacant position at another school.

He says the more than 20 affected heads of schools are within the Suva Education District, which also covers areas including Namosi, Serua, Beqa and Yanuca.

Manumanunitoga says the Permanent Secretary for Education had been invited to the conference to respond to issues raised by teachers but was unable to attend because of other commitments and sent a representative.

He says while the representative tried to explain what had happened, the FTA believes the officials responsible for the decisions should have been present to answer the teachers' concerns.

Manumanunitoga says the Ministry made the mistake and now needs to find a solution for the affected teachers.

The teachers received their revocation letters last week and, according to Manumanunitoga, are expected to be redeployed or return to their substantive positions when school resumes next term.

The FTA Annual Delegates Conference brings together delegates from the Association’s 87 branches around the country.

We have sent questions to the Ministry of Education and are awaiting their response.

item.title: More than 150 killed, hundreds missing after devastating Nepal floods
item.description: More than 150 people have been killed and hundreds remain missing after a massive flash flood and mudslide struck Nepal. According to Nepal’s tourist board, those missing include more than 100 tourists from India, 54 from the United States and 33 from the United Kingdom.
item.content:encoded:
More than 150 people have been killed and hundreds remain missing after a massive flash flood and mudslide struck Nepal.

According to Nepal’s tourist board, those missing include more than 100 tourists from India, 54 from the United States and 33 from the United Kingdom.

More than 100 Nepalese are also reported missing, along with dozens of police officers, army personnel and power workers.

Authorities had initially considered whether an earthquake triggered the disaster, but the US Geological Survey says the seismic energy detected was generated by a landslide.

Search and rescue efforts are continuing.
